title: Format prompt templates in a single pass (escaped braces, rescanned values, backslashes)

files.patch:
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@
 - [SECURITY]: A change which fixes a security vulnerability.
 
 ## [Unreleased]
+- [BUGFIX] [https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb/pull/1056] Format `PromptTemplate` and the `FewShotPromptTemplate` suffix in a single pass, so escaped `{{braces}}` stay literal, an inserted value is never expanded as another variable, and backslashes in values (`\'`, `\0`, `\&`) are kept as-is.
 - [BUGFIX] [https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb/pull/1055] Stop sending the default `temperature` (0.0) from `Langchain::LLM::Anthropic#chat`; Claude Opus 4.7+ and Sonnet 5+ reject it with a 400. A temperature set in `default_options` or passed to `#chat` is still sent.
 - [BUGFIX] [https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb/pull/1052] Return every `tool_use` block from `AnthropicResponse#tool_calls` instead of only the first, so parallel tool calls from Claude are no longer silently dropped.
 - [BUGFIX] [https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb/pull/1051] Skip unsupported and non-file directory entries when loading a directory instead of returning an `UnknownFormatError` object into the results array.

@@ -90,8 +90,11 @@ def initialize(
     def format(**kwargs)
       example_string = @examples.map { |example| @example_prompt.format(**example) }
 
-      suffix_string = @suffix
-      kwargs.each { |key, value| suffix_string = suffix_string.gsub(/\{#{key}\}/, value.to_s) }
+      values = kwargs.transform_keys(&:to_s)
+      # A single pass, so an inserted value is never rescanned for variables or backslash escapes.
+      suffix_string = @suffix.gsub(/\{([^{}]*)\}/) do |match|
+        values.fetch(Regexp.last_match(1)) { match }.to_s
+      end
 
       [@prefix, *example_string, suffix_string].join(@example_separator)
     end

@@ -57,10 +57,17 @@ def initialize(template:, input_variables:, validate_template: true)
     # @return [String] A formatted string.
     #
     def format(**kwargs)
-      result = @template
-      result = result.gsub(/{{/, "{").gsub(/}}/, "}")
-      kwargs.each { |key, value| result = result.gsub(/\{#{key}\}/, value.to_s) }
-      result
+      values = kwargs.transform_keys(&:to_s)
+      # A single pass over the template: `{{` and `}}` become literal braces instead of opening a
+      # variable, and an inserted value is never rescanned, so braces or backslashes in it
+      # (JSON, code, user input) come out unchanged.
+      @template.gsub(/\{\{|\}\}|\{([^{}]*)\}/) do |match|
+        case match
+        when "{{" then "{"
+        when "}}" then "}"
+        else values.fetch(Regexp.last_match(1)) { match }.to_s
+        end
+      end
     end

+
+    it "keeps escaped braces literal when their content is also a variable name" do
+      prompt = described_class.new(template: "Write {{name}} literally, then {name}.", input_variables: ["name"])
+
+      expect(prompt.format(name: "Ada")).to eq("Write {name} literally, then Ada.")
+    end
+
+    it "does not expand a variable that appears inside another variable's value" do
+      prompt = described_class.new(template: "Question: {question} Context: {context}", input_variables: ["question", "context"])
+
+      expect(prompt.format(question: "what is {context}?", context: "internal notes"))
+        .to eq("Question: what is {context}? Context: internal notes")
+    end
+
+    it "inserts values with backslashes unchanged" do
+      prompt = described_class.new(template: "Code: {code}", input_variables: ["code"])
+      code = %q(s = 'It\'s'; re = /\d+/; path = "C:\\Users"; m = "\0\&")
+
+      expect(prompt.format(code: code)).to eq("Code: #{code}")
+    end
